content.user_title: Design Apple Layout and Navigation Patterns
content.value_statement: Choosing the right Apple layout pattern can be difficult across iPhone, iPad, Mac, and visionOS. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code HIG-based guidance for navigation, split views, sidebars, tabs, windows, panels, and ornaments.
actual_capabilities: Recommends tab bars, sidebars, split views, column views, windows, panels, and ornaments based on app structure.
Maps navigation choices across iPhone, iPad, Mac, watchOS, tvOS, and visionOS guidance where referenced.
Provides a layout adaptation checklist for compact width, regular width, multitasking, accessibility, orientation, and visionOS.
References local Markdown guidance for boxes, lists, tables, scroll views, tabs, windows, and related components.
Defines an output format covering navigation pattern, layout hierarchy, platform adaptation, and size class behavior.
limitations: It summarizes Apple HIG guidance but does not replace the current Apple documentation.
It does not inspect running apps or validate implementation details automatically.
It does not provide full accessibility testing, device testing, or legal compliance review.
It focuses on layout and navigation, not visual branding or detailed component styling.

use_cases.title: Choose Navigation Architecture
use_cases.description: A product designer compares tabs, sidebars, and split views before a new Apple app flow is finalized.

use_cases.title: Adapt Layouts Across Platforms
use_cases.description: An iOS developer plans how an iPhone navigation stack expands on iPad, Mac, or visionOS.

use_cases.title: Review Interface Structure
use_cases.description: A design lead checks whether windows, panels, lists, and tables follow expected platform conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Recommend a Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to recommend an Apple navigation pattern for an app with [number] top-level sections, [hierarchy depth], and target platforms [platforms]. Explain the rationale and tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Platform Adaptation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to map my current [iPhone, iPad, or Mac] layout to [target platforms]. Include size class behavior, sidebar rules, and tab behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Navigation Proposal
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review this navigation proposal: [paste summary]. Identify HIG alignment issues for sidebars, lists, split views, tabs, windows, and scroll views.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Adaptation Specification
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to produce a platform adaptation spec for [app]. Include root hierarchy, component selection, compact and regular transitions, multitasking behavior, and visionOS window or ornament guidance.

output_examples.input: A task app has four top-level sections and must support iPhone and iPad.
output: Use a bottom tab bar on iPhone for the four peer sections.
Use an adaptable sidebar on iPad when the sections need labels, grouping, or customization.
Keep detail navigation inside each section so tab selection remains stable.

output_examples.input: A document editor needs an inspector, a canvas, and a file browser on Mac.
output: Use a main window with a sidebar for files, a central canvas, and an inspector panel or split pane.
Keep the inspector focused on the current selection and update it as the selection changes.
Avoid opening extra windows by default unless the user asks for a separate document view.

output_examples.input: A visionOS app needs controls that stay near a window without blocking content.
output: Use an ornament for frequently needed controls that should remain near the window.
Keep the ornament narrow enough to avoid competing with side tabs or toolbars.
Prefer one additional ornament when possible to reduce visual weight.

best_practices: Provide platform targets, hierarchy depth, and number of top-level sections before asking for recommendations.
Ask for compact and regular width behavior when planning iPhone and iPad layouts.
Use the output as design guidance, then validate in Apple documentation and device testing.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to replace current Apple documentation for final release decisions.
Do not use one navigation pattern for every platform without checking adaptation rules.
Do not treat layout guidance as accessibility, performance, or implementation validation.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps choose Apple layout and navigation components such as tabs, sidebars, split views, windows, panels, lists, and ornaments.

faq.question: Which platforms does it cover?
faq.answer: It includes guidance for iPhone, iPad, Mac, watchOS, tvOS, and visionOS where the referenced HIG pages discuss them.

faq.question: Can it write SwiftUI or UIKit code?
faq.answer: It can guide component choices and hierarchy, but the skill content is design guidance rather than a code generator.

faq.question: Does it replace Apple documentation?
faq.answer: No. Use it for planning and review, then verify final decisions with current Apple documentation and platform testing.

faq.question: What input should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide your app structure, platform targets, hierarchy depth, top-level sections, and any multitasking or visionOS needs.

faq.question: Is this useful for design reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare a proposed navigation structure with HIG guidance and identify layout risks or platform mismatches.
